question: How do the directly inspected Palaima and Owens arguments differ over the script assignment of the Knossos painted wall sign?

sources.citation: Thomas G. Palaima (1981), On the Painted Linear Sign from a Wall at Knossos, Kadmos 20, 79–82.
sources.rights: Copyrighted source; public academic offprint access does not confer a bulk reuse licence. Original short attributed comparison notes only; no source text, figure, facsimile or reconstructed edition is redistributed.

sources.citation: Gareth Owens, Three Re-discovered Linear A Inscriptions from Knossos, Minos 25–26 (1990–1991), 367–372.
sources.rights: No source PDF/images/edition transcription redistributed. Only original source-attributed comparison notes and bibliographic locators are admitted.

consultation_pages.inspection: Text and rendered page checked, including footnote7

claims.locator: pp.80–81, especially p.81 comparison and reversal paragraphs
claims.assertion: Palaima favours Linear B using reversed-sign parallels and formal comparison. He also discusses possible Linear A explanations and the lack of an exact stratigraphic context.

claims.locator: p.370, KN Zd46 section and footnote7; p.371 concluding paragraph
claims.assertion: Owens proposes Linear A admission for the painted fragment, discussing its medium and style. Footnote7 explicitly acknowledges Palaima’s different attribution.

comparison.basis: Owens identifies the Knossos fresco fragment and explicitly cites Palaima1981 on that fragment in footnote7. This establishes the shared subject of the arguments, not present-day physical identity.
comparison.native_join_scope: No exact KN Zd46 entry was found in the admitted 802-row SigLA document view. Do not create a canonical record or fuzzy join.
comparison.source_dependence: Both arguments concern one fragment and shared earlier publications. Owens engages Palaima. Different scholarly opinions are not independent object witnesses.
comparison.gorila_firewall: No GORILA readings, sign tables, images or derivative reconstruction are admitted. Only these authors’ original arguments about the fragment and bibliographic locators are recorded. Their other GORILA-dependent comparisons are excluded.
